101.name: Doe v. Roe
101.raw_text: In this action the plaintiff sued for the price of rooms let by the night. The court below found that the lodger has not the possession, but the use only, and that the householder retained the control and the keys of every chamber so let. Judgment for the plaintiff is accordingly affirmed.

102.name: Smith v. Jones
102.raw_text: This was a suit upon a promissory note given for the purchase of a threshing machine. Nothing in the record touches the letting of rooms or lodgings, and the single question is one of consideration.

201.name: Board v. Keller
201.raw_text: The defendant kept a boarding house in the city of Cleveland, and the occupants dwelt there by the month under an arrangement terminable at will. The ordinance in question forbids such a use in a residence district.

202.name: State v. Prentiss
202.raw_text: The rule is ancient and is not doubted: the innkeeper is bound to receive all comers, and for that reason the law has always dealt with his calling otherwise than with the letting of a dwelling.
